subject: Priv infra CI: GitOps workflow, Helm hooks, and Ansible playbook review
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-analytics.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@cloudpartner.io
Date: 2026-12-20T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Private deployment CI review - GitOps + Helm hooks + Ansible playbooks

Hi team,

Thanks again for taking time to review our private deployment automation. We've been iterating on the GitOps pipeline and added a Helm chart (privstack) and an Ansible playbook that prepares on-prem nodes for GPU drivers and kernel tuning.

High-level asks:
- Quick pass on the GitHub Actions workflow for safety (rollbacks, approvals).
- Helm hooks: pre-upgrade job for KV cache migration, and post-upgrade smoke tests. Is the hook timing safe with our PV rotation?
- Ansible: idempotency and dry-run coverage; we attached acme-ansible-playbook-v2.yaml.

Attachments: acme-ansible-playbook-v2.yaml, helm-chart-privstack-1.4.0.tgz, gitops-pipeline-diagram.pdf

I can join a 30m sync if that helps — suggested times tomorrow 10:00 or 16:00 PT.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai, ops@cloudpartner.io
Date: 2026-12-20T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment CI review - GitOps + Helm hooks + Ansible playbooks

Sanjay — thanks for the packet and diagram. Quick read-through and initial notes below; I'll follow-up with inline suggestions in the GitHub PR.

Top-level items:
1) GitOps workflow: enforce a required approver group for any chart/image updates to the priv namespace; add an automated canary promotion step.
2) Helm hooks: pre-upgrade jobs are fine, but they must run with the same RBAC and service account as the release to access PVs; ensure the hook has an ownerReference so the chart garbage collection handles failures cleanly.
3) Ansible playbook: I saw a couple places where shell: | blocks assume non-interactive apt installs — add explicit --no-install-recommends and a check to avoid re-running driver installs if already present. Use tags so dry-run can focus on kernel-tune vs driver install.

Please vote for the 10:00 slot if the team is good; I'll block 30m. I'll add specific line comments in the PR and attach a small sample GitHub Actions snippet for an approval gate.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-analytics.com>, markus_klein@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-20T10:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment CI review - GitOps + Helm hooks + Ansible playbooks

Looping in a couple of CI/ops guardrails I want enforced before we approve GA deployment:
- Pipeline must have a reversible migration path: store KV-schema version in a ConfigMap and check pre/post values in smoke tests.
- Add a feature-flagged fast-fail step in Actions to catch image digest mismatches (prevent drift between chart values and container registry).
- Secret management: ensure Helm chart references external secret provider (Vault/KMS) via value files and does not contain inline credentials.

I also recommend the following quick changes to the GitOps repo layout: move helm values for onprem into a separate values-onprem.yaml and add a templated secrets.example.yaml to make reviews easier.

I'll add a small workflow to the shared infra repo that enforces a manual approval stage for production promotion (cannot be skipped).

Laura Bennett
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-analytics.com>, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-12-20T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment CI review - GitOps + Helm hooks + Ansible playbooks

A few Helm-specific gotchas from my read of the chart tarball:
- The pre-upgrade hook currently runs as a Job without a backoffLimit. If the migration job touches large KV stores, it should have a conservative backoff (e.g., backoffLimit: 0 and ttlSecondsAfterFinished set so we don't retry forever).
- Use helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation to avoid stale job artifacts between releases.
- Post-upgrade smoke test should include a readiness probe check and a lightweight query to the model-serving endpoint (healthz) — don't rely solely on pod status.

Also: make sure the chart templates avoid using include/indent combos that break when rendered as part of umbrella charts. I found one template that will render an empty string if values.onprem is missing — add defaults.

Markus Klein
Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment CI review - GitOps + Helm hooks + Ansible playbooks

Couple of additions focused on testability and rollout safety:
- Add a staged rollout job in the GitOps pipeline that promotes to 2 nodes first (canary) and runs the full smoke test set before scaling to the rest.
- Ansible: add a local --check run as part of the pipeline and gate actual runs behind an explicit manual confirmation for prod hosts. Tag hosts with "gpu-ready" during onboarding so playbooks can be idempotent.
- Observability: emit a deploy-trace ID as an annotation on the release and propagate that into smoke tests so we can correlate failures with CI runs.

I'll prepare a short snippet for the pipeline that adds the staged rollout and the --check step; pushing that to the review branch shortly.

Mina Haddad
Release Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme-analytics.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment CI review - GitOps + Helm hooks + Ansible playbooks

Fantastic feedback — appreciate the fast turnaround. We've pushed two small changes to the PR:
- Adjusted Helm hook backoff/ttl and added hook-delete-policy.
- Split values-onprem.yaml and removed embedded secrets.
- Added tags to the playbook and a --check dry-run path; attached updated playbook: acme-ansible-playbook-v2.yaml (rev B).

Next steps for us: incorporate your GH Actions snippet (Karthik), apply the staged rollout (Mina), and we can schedule a 30m smoke window next week to validate with our ops team and CloudOps partner.

I'll also attach the updated diagram to the PR and include the Drive link.

Thanks all — ping me if you'd like a short walkthrough.

Sanjay Rao
Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics
